services.title: NIOS-X Anycast API
services.description:
The anycast capability enables the HA (High Availability) configuration of NIOS-X applications that run on equipment located on a customer's premises (on-prem hosts). Anycast supports DNS as well as DNS-forwarding services.

Anycast-enabled application setups use multiple on-premises installations for one particular application type. Multiple application instances are configured to use the same endpoint address. Anycast capability is collocated with such an application instance, for monitoring the local application instance and advertising to the upstream router (a customer's equipment) a per-instance, local route to the common application endpoint address, as long as the local application instance is available. Depending on the type of the upstream router, the customer may configure local route advertisement via the BGP (Boarder Gateway Protocol) or OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocols. Both protocols may be enabled as well. Multiple routes to the common application service address provide redundancy without the need to reconfigure application clients.

Should an application instance become unavailable, the local route advertisements stop. This results in withdrawal of the route (in the upstream router) to the application instance that has gone out of service and ensures that subsequent application requests get routed to the remaining available application instances.

services.title: Infoblox Cloud DFP API
services.description:
Infoblox Cloud is a SaaS offering designed to provide protection to devices on and off premises, such as roaming, remote, and branch offices. It provides visibility into infected and compromised devices, prevents DNS-based data exfiltration, and automatically stops device communications with command-and-control servers and botnets, in addition to providing recursive DNS services in the cloud. You can access the services by deploying the Infoblox Endpoint agent or the DNS forwarding proxy.

You can use a DNS Forwarding Proxy in scenarios where an endpoint agent is to be deployed in a remote office or where installing an agent is not desirable or possible. A DNS Forwarding Proxy runs on bare metal, VM infrastructures, and Infoblox NIOS appliances, and it embeds the client IPs in DNS queries before forwarding them to Infoblox Cloud. The communications are encrypted, and client visibility is maintained. The proxy also provides DNS resolution to local DNS zones when you configure local resolvers. Once you set up a DNS Forwarding Proxy, it becomes the main DNS server for your remote site. It will also cache responses to speed up resolution of future queries.

After implementing the DNS Forwarding Proxy, you can rest assured that Infoblox Cloud effectively enforces DNS client–based security policies at your remote sites. On-premises devices that send DNS queries reveal their actual client IP addresses (instead of their NAT IP addresses), and this allows Infoblox Cloud to apply the security policies applicable to the respective endpoints and to identify infected clients.

services.title: Infoblox EndPoint API
services.description:
Infoblox Endpoint is a lightweight roaming agent that redirects DNS traffic from your remote devices to Infoblox Cloud. It enables you to apply appropriate security policies to your roaming end users in remote sites and branch offices.

For end users to connect to Infoblox cloud services, you must download and install Infoblox Endpoint on the users' devices. The client enforces security policies that you apply to the remote networks, regardless of where your end users are and which networks they are connected to. Infoblox Endpoint listens on port 53 of the device. If other software listens on the same port, DNS traffic cannot be redirected to Infoblox Cloud and your device will not be protected by Infoblox Endpoint.

When you use Infoblox Endpoint, DNS queries are sent to Infoblox Cloud directly in all scenarios except those where (1) queries target the bypassed domains and (2) internal domains are collected through the DHCP server. If you have internal domains served by your local DNS servers and you want to reach them without interruptions, consider adding them to the bypassed internal domains list; this will ensure that DNS queries for these internal domains get sent to the local DNS servers rather than Infoblox Cloud.

Infoblox Endpoint supports dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 DNS configurations, thereby protecting all devices, regardless of their network environments. Infoblox Endpoint in a dual-stack environment can proxy IPv6 DNS queries and forward them to Infoblox Cloud over IPv4.

services.title: Infoblox FW API

An extension of the Infoblox Suite, Infoblox Threat Defense Cloud provides visibility into infected and compromised off-premises devices, roaming users, remote sites, and branch offices. You can subscribe to Infoblox Cloud and use its functionality to mitigate and control malware, provide unprecedented insight into your network security posture, and enable timely action. Infoblox Cloud also offers unified policy management, reporting, and threat analytics across the entire spectrum. Using automated and high-quality threat intelligence feeds and unique behavioral analytics, it automatically stops device communications with C&Cs/botnets and prevents DNS-based data exfiltration.

The mission-critical DNS infrastructure can become a vulnerable component in your network when it is inadequately protected by traditional security solutions and, consequently, used as an attack surface. Compromise of DNS services can result in catastrophic failures in the network and system. To fully protect your network in today’s cyber-security threat environment, Infoblox sets a new DNS security standard by offering scalable, integrated enterprise-grade protection for your DNS infrastructure.

Use the Infoblox Cloud Services Portal to view the status of your subscription and threat-intelligence feeds and to manage your network scope and roaming end users. Use the Infoblox Threat Lookup tool and predefined reports to learn about threats in your networks.

services.description:
<!-- edit this in swagger_description.md file and then run `make swagger` to update the JSON -->

Infoblox WAPI is a service specifically designed to streamline WAPI access to a federated NIOS grid using the Infoblox Portal API endpoint (https://wapi.csp.infoblox.com). To start leveraging its functionalities, it is essential to include two critical headers: `license_uid` and `Authorization`.

- `license_uid`: To find the license_uid (identifier for the grid) in the Infoblox Portal, follow these steps:

  1. Log into the Infoblox Portal and navigate to the **Manage** tab.
  2. Under Manage, go to the **Infrastructure** section.
  3. Under respective NIOS host card, you can see the license UID.
  Additional information on obtaining License uid from NIOS is available at https://docs.infoblox.com/space/nios86/35759169/show+license_uid.

- `Authorization`: This header needs to be set with an identity token, such as a Service API Key. Please note that the Infoblox Portal user must have the appropriate NIOS WAPI permissions.

### Permissions in Infoblox Portal to Allow WAPI Access
- `NIOS WAPI Passthrough CSP - Create`: Allow HTTP POST API
- `NIOS WAPI Passthrough CSP - Read`: Allow HTTP GET on a WAPI object 
- `NIOS WAPI Passthrough CSP - List`: Allow HTTP GET on a WAPI object-type
- `NIOS WAPI Passthrough CSP - Update`: Allow HTTP PUT API
- `NIOS WAPI Passthrough CSP - Delete`: Allow HTTP DELETE API

### Default Roles with Above Permissions
- NIOS Manager Role: all permissions
- NIOS Viewer Role: read and list permissions
- Administrator Role: all permissions
- User Role: read and list permissions
- DDI Administrator Role: all permissions
- DDI User Role: read and list permissions

For information on WAPI endpoints, please refer to the WAPI documentation at the following URL: `https://<nios-ip>/wapidoc/index.html`. Please replace `<nios-ip>` with your actual NIOS host IP address.

### Exclusion

1. Only WAPI APIs that are supported by the NIOS grid are included and other APIs are excluded. The WAPI API path begins with `/wapi` followed by the WAPI version. For example, `/wapi/v2.12.3`. Infoblox WAPI supports all versions that are available on NIOS and are documented in the WAPI documentation of your grid.
2. Long running APIs (like grid restore API) are excluded.

Below are some examples of making requests through Infoblox WAPI.

Before using the API to query metrics, you must complete the following steps in the Cloud Services Portal: * Create a service account and assign a custom role with the Customer Metrics permission, which grants access to the endpoint * Create a service API key by using the created service account * Use the service API key to access the endpoint. services.title: DNS Configuration API
services.description:
DNS Configuration API for managing DNS zones, views, servers, hosts, and security policies. Response Policy Zones (RPZs) are also managed through this API under the /dns/rpz endpoints — use these to list, create, and manage Local RPZ policies on NIOS-X. Do NOT use NIOS WAPI passthrough (B1wapiService) for RPZ queries; use this API instead.

Resource identifiers in this service are opaque, namespaced values of the form `<service>/<type>/<uuid>` (e.g. `dns/view/abc123`, `dns/auth_zone/def456`). The type prefix is part of the value — never strip it, add it, or reconstruct an identifier from a bare UUID. Foreign-key fields such as `view`, `parent`, or `nsgs` already contain the full canonical identifier as returned by the API; use them exactly as-is. To determine whether two identifiers refer to the same resource, compare the complete strings for exact equality — do not transform them or issue additional queries to test equality.

RPZ (Response Policy Zone) guidance: Use /dns/rpz to list, create, read, update, or delete RPZ zones. Do NOT use WAPI or B1wapiService for RPZ operations — all RPZ management is available via this DnsConfig API. RPZ rules (policy records) are DNS records stored under the RPZ zone and are retrieved via the DnsData service /dns/record endpoint filtered by zone id.

It is part of the full-featured, DDI cloud solution that enables customers to deploy large numbers of protocol servers to deliver DNS and DHCP throughout their enterprise network. 



Resource identifiers in this service are opaque, namespaced values of the form `<service>/<type>/<uuid>` (e.g. `dns/record/abc123`, `dns/auth_zone/def456`). The type prefix is part of the value — never strip it, add it, or reconstruct an identifier from a bare UUID. Foreign-key fields such as `zone` and `view` already contain the full canonical identifier as returned by the API; use them exactly as-is. To determine whether two identifiers refer to the same resource, compare the complete strings for exact equality — do not transform them or issue additional queries to test equality.

RPZ record listing — IMPORTANT: When listing records for an RPZ zone, always filter by zone id: _filter=zone=='<rpz_zone_id>' where the zone id comes from the /dns/rpz response (e.g. dns/rpz/abc123). Do NOT issue an unfiltered /dns/record call to retrieve RPZ rules — it will fail in accounts that contain SVCB/HTTPS records (error: SVCB/HTTPS target_name must not be empty). RPZ policy rule records have source containing 'RPZRULE' — exclude system-generated NS and SOA records (source 'SYSTEM') when presenting rules to the user.

- **DNS servers**: `dns` (NIOS-X cloud) and `ndns` (NIOS on-prem grid) are both DNS. When a user asks about DNS servers, hosts, or check-in times, ALWAYS query for BOTH `dns` AND `ndns` service types.
- **DHCP servers**: `dhcp` (NIOS-X cloud) and `ndhcp` (NIOS on-prem grid) are both DHCP. When a user asks about DHCP servers, hosts, or check-in times, ALWAYS query for BOTH `dhcp` AND `ndhcp` service types.

Users typically want to see all servers regardless of whether they are cloud or on-prem. Never filter to only one variant when showing lists of DNS or DHCP servers.

---


### Hosts API

The Hosts API is used to manage the Infrastructure Host resources.
These include the operations related to hosts, such as viewing, creation, update, replacement, disconnection, and deletion of hosts.
Hosts are managed from the Cloud Services Portal -> Manage -> Infrastructure -> the Hosts tab.

**Host IP address fields — label these correctly:** Each host (NIOS-X server) exposes exactly two IP address fields: `ip_address` is the host's **Server IP Address** (the IP configured on the server's own network interface) and `nat_ip` is the host's **NAT IP Address** (the NAT-translated address). NIOS-X servers do NOT have a separate 'management IP' or 'LAN IP' field. 'WAN' and 'LAN' are per-interface roles — they separate management traffic (between the server and the Cloud Services Portal) from service/data traffic and are configured under a server's IP Interface Settings, not host-level fields returned by these APIs. When a user asks for a host's IP in 'management', 'LAN', 'WAN', 'WAN interface', 'LAN interface', or any per-interface terms — however phrased, and even if they explicitly ask for such columns — the result table or list MUST NOT contain any column, field, or heading whose name contains or implies 'WAN', 'LAN', or 'management'. This is an absolute rule with no exceptions. IQ Agent exposes only two IP fields per host: present `ip_address` as the **Server IP Address** and `nat_ip` as the **NAT IP Address**, and NEVER relabel, rename, or map either field to a WAN, LAN, or management IP (neither in a column nor in prose). Do NOT leave WAN/LAN columns blank, do NOT call, search for, or route to any other service to obtain per-interface IPs, and do NOT claim this data does not exist or is unavailable — it is simply outside what IQ Agent surfaces. Alongside the two-field result, include a plain sentence such as: 'IQ Agent provides each server's Server IP and NAT IP; a per-interface WAN/LAN IP breakdown is not available through IQ Agent.'

---


### Services API

The Services API is used to manage the Infrastructure Service resources, also known as NIOS-X applications.
These include the operations for viewing, creating, updating, starting/stopping, configuring, and deleting services.
Services are managed from the Cloud Services Portal (CSP) by navigating to Manage -> Infrastructure -> the Services tab.

---


### Detail APIs

The Detail APIs are the read-only APIs used to list all Infrastructure resources: hosts and services.
Each resource record returned also contains information about its associated resource(s) and the
status information (the Host/Service status) for itself and the associated resource(s).

---



Resource identifiers in this service are opaque, namespaced values of the form `<service>/<type>/<uuid>` (e.g. `dns/record/abc123`, `dns/auth_zone/def456`). The type prefix is part of the value — never strip it, add it, or reconstruct an identifier from a bare UUID. The Notifications Mailbox API provides access to user and account-level alerts and notifications generated by Infoblox Portal services.

IMPORTANT — there is NO host_id, resource_id, or structured host reference in alert responses. The fields service_id and service_data are currently always null.

To answer questions about notifications or alerts for a specific host, connection, or resource:
1. Fetch ALL alerts using make_get_request with fetch_all=True on /user_alerts or /account_alerts.
2. Use the table_name returned by make_get_request (e.g. notifications_mailbox_user_alerts_get.parquet) in the query_stored_data SQL — do NOT guess or hardcode the filename.
3. Use query_stored_data with a SQL ILIKE filter on the message and subject fields. Example: SELECT * FROM notifications_mailbox_user_alerts_get.parquet WHERE message ILIKE '%<hostname>%' OR subject ILIKE '%<hostname>%'
4. If the search term contains a single quote, escape it by doubling it (e.g. O''Brien becomes O''Brien in the SQL string).

Do NOT attempt to filter by host_id or resource_id — these fields do not exist. Do NOT use any other API or service to find host-related alerts.

services.title: TIDE Data Service
services.description:
The heart of TIDE is the threats submitted by the Infoblox Cyber Intelligence group and external partners.

There are two main categories of bulk threat data retrievable in TIDE: threat state and threats by age. Threat state consists of records that are considered current threats, that is, threats that have not expired and have not been superseded by newer threats for the same indicator (host name, IP address, URL, hash, or email). Threats by age consists of all threats submitted in a specified time period.

If the same indicator was submitted by a data provider four times in one day, a threats-by-age call for daily results would return four records, while a threat state call would return only one, the most recent one submitted.

TIDE threat data is generally event oriented. Sometimes it is necessary instead to see threats by their current state, that is, threats that have not expired and have not been superseded by newer threats for the same indicator (host name, IP address, URL, hash, or email).

The materialized threat state objects contain the current active threats for all indicators of the specified record type. Threat state objects are materialized multiple times an hour.

POST.summary: Create Dossier lookup job(s) (one or more indicator)
POST.description:
The Create Dossier Lookup Job(s) API returns detailed information on the specified indicator(s) from the requested sources. By default the call returns task and job IDs for each requested source which can be queried with other Dossier (Intel Lookup) endpoints while they work in the background. To have the API return the results when complete, specify ‘wait=true’ in the request parameters. There are three available formats for the request body, only one of them should be used at a time. The "one" request body searches a single indicator against multiple sources. The "group" request body searches multiple indicators of the same target type against multiple sources. The "list" request body searches multiple indicators of different target types against multiple sources.

Request body variables:
- type : indicator type, available values : host, ip, url, hash, email
- target : string indicator to look up ("targets" when object is "group")
- sources : list of lookup sources
